metadata.title: Mednarodna raziskava računalniške in informacijske pismenosti (IEA ICILS 2023) : nacionalno poročilo - prvi rezultati

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The report is a national ICILS 2023 results report based on IEA’s international large-scale assessment design with clustered two-stage sampling (schools, then classes/sections within schools). It describes that results are reported for the target population of Grade 8 students and that the international reporting uses sampling weights and complex survey procedures to produce representative estimates and standard errors; however, the national report does not explicitly name the weight variables (e.g., W_FSTUWT) or replicate-weight method (e.g., BRR/jackknife). Plausible values are used for the achievement scales (RI literacy and optional CT/CT-related scale), and the report notes that the reported country means are not simple averages of student raw scores, but population estimates derived from plausible values under the complex design. For this extraction, weights and replicate weights are therefore left as null because the manuscript does not provide the exact technical weight variable names or replication scheme.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The report clearly states that ICILS achievement results are produced using plausible values (PVs) for the RI literacy and RM/CT achievement scales, but it does not document the missing-data strategy for the student questionnaire and background variables (e.g., whether cases with missing background data were excluded, imputed, or handled via multiple imputation). This is a reporting gap for methodological transparency because ICILS datasets typically contain missingness in background questionnaires and nonresponse, and the report does not specify how that missingness was treated in the national analyses.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The report uses ICILS 2023 for Slovenia and describes a representative sample for the target population of Grade 8 students. The sampling is clustered two-stage: first schools are sampled with probability proportional to size, then one class/section is sampled within each school (with all teachers in the target grade included for teacher questionnaires, reflecting the subject-integrated nature of RI literacy/RM). The report also notes that during sampling/fieldwork some exclusions occur (e.g., private schools excluded for the international reporting; students who could not complete instruments due to language/technical issues are excluded), and that missing data were handled in the international reporting process, but the exact national analytic inclusion/exclusion rules for missing questionnaire items are not specified in the provided text.

data.outcome_summary: This national ICILS 2023 report presents first results for Slovenia on two achievement constructs: computer and information literacy (RI literacy/CIL) and computer thinking (RM/CT, optional module). The assessment uses computer-based, authentic modules: RI literacy is measured with seven 30-minute modules rotated across students (each student completes two modules), while RM is measured with four 25-minute modules rotated across students (each student completes two modules). Achievement scales are reported on an IEA metric with a mean of 500 and SD of 100 for the international reference, and country means are derived using plausible values rather than raw test-score averages. The report also provides distributional information (percentiles and proficiency levels) and contextual comparisons (e.g., gender, immigrant background, language at home, SES proxies such as parental education and books at home, and access to devices at home). Methodologically, it emphasizes that reported scores are population estimates for the school system and that PV-based scaling is required for valid comparisons; however, the national report does not specify the exact missing-data handling procedure for background variables.
